metadata.name: [GCP Compute OTel] CPU saturation across a zone
metadata.description: Alerts when a significant share of the VM fleet in a zone runs at or above 90% of its reserved CPU cores (averaged over 15 minutes). Fleet-level by design: a single busy VM does not page. Returns one row per breaching project and zone with the saturated instance names.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.compute.otel-*
// Compute Engine VM instances only (the data stream also holds instance_group metrics)
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "gce_instance"
    AND `compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization` IS NOT NULL
// Per-VM average CPU utilisation over the lookback window.
// utilization is a fraction of RESERVED cores and can exceed 1.0 on shared-core / burstable types.
// OTel TSDS splits one entity's metric into several series (_metric_names_hash is a dimension),
// so per-entity means are SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME) / SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME), never SUM/MAX of AVG_OVER_TIME.
| STATS
    cpu_sum = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization`)),
    cpu_n = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization`))
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone, resource.attributes.instance_id, attributes.instance_name
| WHERE cpu_n > 0
| EVAL cpu_util = TO_DOUBLE(cpu_sum) / cpu_n
// Per-VM saturation threshold (fraction of reserved cores). Tune to your workload headroom policy.
| EVAL is_saturated = cpu_util >= 0.9
// Roll up to the zone: how much of the fleet is saturated?
| STATS
    instances = COUNT(*),
    saturated_instances = COUNT(*) WHERE is_saturated,
    zone_avg_cpu_util = ROUND(AVG(cpu_util), 3),
    max_cpu_util = ROUND(MAX(cpu_util), 3),
    saturated_instance_names = VALUES(attributes.instance_name) WHERE is_saturated
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.zone
| EVAL saturated_pct = ROUND(saturated_instances * 100.0 / instances, 1)

data.content:
## CPU saturation across a zone

A large share of the Compute Engine VMs in this zone are running at or above 90% of their reserved CPU cores (15-minute average). This signals fleet-wide capacity pressure, not a single busy VM.

### Triage
1. Check whether `scheduler_wait_time` (CPU steal) is also elevated in the zone. High utilisation with near-zero steal points to workload growth; high steal points to host contention (see the CPU steal rule).
2. Compare network and disk throughput for the saturated instances. Rising traffic alongside CPU confirms organic load growth.
3. If the instances belong to a managed instance group, check whether the autoscaler reached its maximum size or is configured with too high a CPU target.
4. Look for recent deployments or batch jobs that started across the fleet.

### Remediation
Scale out (raise the MIG max size or add instances), resize to a larger machine type, or rebalance workloads to other zones.

### Tuning
`cpu_util >= 0.9` sets the per-VM threshold. `saturated_pct >= 20 AND saturated_instances >= 2` sets the fleet condition. Values above 1.0 are normal on shared-core (E2 micro/small/medium) VMs during bursts. GCP Cloud Monitoring metrics typically arrive several minutes late, so the most recent minutes of the lookback window may be empty; the window is sized to tolerate this.
